findings.body: When `text` is longer than `limit` and the first `limit` characters contain no space, `head` is exactly `limit` characters and the `None` branch appends `…`, yielding `limit + 1` characters. The doc comment promises "at most `limit` characters," and the stated callers (GitHub check-run titles, finding titles) enforce hard ceilings — exceeding the limit defeats the purpose of the function. Concrete input: `shorten("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz", 20)` returns `"abcdefghijklmnopqrst…"` (21 chars). Reserving one character for the ellipsis in `head` fixes both branches without exceeding the limit.
findings.title: Reserve one character for the ellipsis in shorten

value.summary: The `shorten` function can return `limit + 1` characters when the first `limit` characters contain no space, violating its documented contract of "at most `limit` characters"; otherwise the change looks sound.
